# Conventions — idle-base

<!-- generated by /kb-generate — last_crawl_commit: ece8760a02e784dba77a283ca07e2c1a39273b81 -->

Everything below is observable in the code today. Where a rule has a canonical example, the
file path is cited — read that file before writing the equivalent.

## Code Style

- **CommonJS throughout**, including in `.js` files containing JSX: `const x = require('./x')`,
  `module.exports = { ... }`. No ESM, no TypeScript, no `import`. Babel handles JSX only.
- No semicolon-free style, no Prettier config in the repo; 2-space indent, single quotes,
  trailing commas in multi-line literals. Lines run to ~110 chars.
- **Comments explain WHY, at length.** This is the single most distinctive thing about the
  codebase. `src/data/acts.js` carries 40-line blocks recording simulation runs behind a tuning
  number; `src/engine/wallBall.js` opens with the invariant it upholds and why. Comments that
  restate the code are not the style — comments that record a decision, a measurement, or a bug
  that was fixed are. Match this or the change will look foreign.
- No linter is configured. There is no `.eslintrc`.

## Testing

- **There is no test runner.** `package.json` declares only `start` and `build`. No `jest`,
  no `vitest`, no test directory.
- The only automated gate is `npm run build` (webpack). It will not catch an
  undefined-dereference on a missing state slice.
- The conventional substitute: **drive the pure engines directly under `node`.** Everything in
  `src/engine/` and `src/data/` is plain CommonJS with no React import, so
  `node -e "require('./src/engine/wallBall')"` works without a build step. Tuning comments
  throughout `src/data/` cite results from exactly this (e.g. "30 runs per band").
- For components, parsing under the repo's own Babel config is the available check.

## File / Module Organization

The three-way split is the architecture:

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| `src/data/` | Config and prose. **No logic.** Every tunable number and every player-facing string. |
| `src/engine/` | Pure logic. **No React, no DOM, no `Date.now()`, no bare `Math.random()`.** |
| `src/components/` | Render only. Decides nothing about rules, costs, odds or availability. |

Corollaries actually enforced in the code:

- A number inline in an engine or component is a bug. It belongs in a `*Config.js`.
- Player-facing prose lives in `src/data/` — see `feedMessages.js`, `toastMessages.js`,
  `storyBeats.js`, `propBetsConfig.js`. A string literal in a component is the same bug.
- Randomness enters an engine as a defaulted parameter (`rng = Math.random`) so behaviour can be
  driven headlessly with a deterministic generator. `engine/wallBall.js` and `engine/bookie.js`
  are the templates.
- Components are one-per-file under a feature folder (`src/components/<feature>/`).

## Naming

- Files: `camelCase.js` for engines/data/actions/hooks; `PascalCase.js` for React components.
- Config files end in `Config.js` (`balanceConfig`, `actFourConfig`, `capsShopConfig`,
  `winPurseConfig`, `modifierKeysConfig`, `walkupSongsConfig`).
- Action types are `SCREAMING_SNAKE` string constants in `state/actionTypes.js`, value === key.
- Action modules are `<feature>Actions.js` exporting named `(state, action)` functions.
- Multipliers end in `Mult` (`revenueMult`, `strengthMult`, `gameSpeedMult`) and are members of
  `BONUS_KEYS` in `data/modifierKeysConfig.js`. A key not in that list is silently inert.
- Clock deadlines end in `AtClock` (`nextGameAtClock`, `nextChallengeAtClock`,
  `completesAtClock`, `nextClickAtClock`) and are compared against `state.clock`, which advances
  1 per second.
- Feature ids in an act's `unlocks` array must equal the `PANELS` key in `AppShell.js` when they
  gate a whole tab.

## Notable Patterns

**Defaulting slice accessors — the most important pattern in the repo.** Saves are persisted to
`localStorage` and **never migrated** (`persistence/saveLoad.js` discards on version mismatch).
So every new state slice is read through an accessor that tolerates its total absence:

```js
function concessionsSlice(state) {
  const slice = (state && state.concessions) || {};
  return { stands: slice.stands || [], boosters: slice.boosters || [], /* … */ };
}
```

Canonical examples: `wallBallSlice()` in `engine/wallBall.js`, `concessionsSlice()` in
`engine/concessions.js`, `capsShopSlice()` in `engine/capsShop.js`, `bookieSlice` in
`engine/bookie.js`, `getTeamName()` in `engine/identity.js`. One `state.newThing.items.map(...)`
white-screens an existing save on load, and the build will not catch it.

**The shop contract.** Every shop engine exposes `listOffers(state)` returning presentation-ready
rows (`{ id, name, description, effect, cost, currency, owned, affordable, count, maxCount }`)
and `purchase(state, id)` returning new state or `null` for refused. The panel renders the rows
verbatim and recomputes nothing. See `engine/lotShop.js` ↔ `components/lot/LotShop.js` as the
reference pair; `concessions`, `wallBallShop`, `sponsorships`, `capsShop` all follow it.

**Refusal is `null` from the engine, unchanged state from the reducer.** An action the player
could not have made through the UI is a no-op, not an error. Several call sites detect "nothing
happened" by reference equality, so return the *identical* object.

**Every wallet write goes through `engine/wallet.js`** (`creditWallet`, `debitWallet`,
`canAfford`, `balanceOf`). No currency may go below zero; this is structural, not a check.

**Derived, never stored.** Unlocked features are recomputed from the act index on every read
(`getUnlockedFeatures`), so retuning an unlock takes effect on an existing save with no
migration. Crew size is *counted* from Respect rather than incremented, so a replayed action
can't double-recruit. Toasts are derived from state transitions in `ToastHost.js` rather than
pushed into state — its header explains why: an 8-hour offline catch-up resolves a whole season
inside one `advance()`, and a stored-toast design fires a storm on load.

**Offline-catch-up safety is a design constraint, not an edge case.** `advance(state, deltaSeconds)`
runs live and on load with only `deltaSeconds` differing, and one iteration can span a whole
season. Anything that fires per-event must be idempotent and must not storm. The house idiom for
"announce once" is a persisted ledger diffed against the current set — `progression.storyBeatsSeen`,
`prestige.victoryAcknowledgedCount`, `sponsorBoard.announcedOfferIds`.

**Two-axis act/era config.** `rules` *replace* a `balanceConfig` value (later layer wins, applied
by spread so a legitimate `0` differs from "absent"); `modifierBonuses` *accumulate* additively
into a clamped multiplier. `resolveRules(state)` and `computeModifiers(state)` in
`engine/modifiers.js` are the only readers. Never read `balanceConfig` directly for a value an act
or era can override — `StandingsPanel.js` resolving `playoffTeams` is the reference.

**Bonuses apply at read time, never by mutating stored values.** `engine/strength.js` applies the
walk-up song multiplier inside `playerOverall` rather than writing to `player.stats`, so a stat
cap can't be laundered through a swap and the card can't disagree with the simulation.

**The manual click is never gated.** `engine/clicker.js` carries the anti-softlock guarantee: the
Hustle button exists in every act and always pays. A cooldown is a rate limit and acceptable; a
gate is not. This is what makes any state recoverable in bounded time, and since the wall-ball
stake cap was removed it is the *only* thing carrying that guarantee.

## Mobile

The game is played on a phone; a 390×844 viewport is the target. `global.css` has a long
`Mobile` section documenting a header that had to be shrunk once already. Tap targets ≥44px,
nothing may scroll the page horizontally, and a `<select>` or text `<input>` needs
`font-size: 16px` or iOS zooms the page on focus. **`global.css` ends inside its
`@media (max-width: 640px)` block** — appending a rule at EOF silently makes it mobile-only.
Feature-scoped section markers near the end of the file are the place to add rules.

## Git

- Feature branches named `story/<slug>`, `feat/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `chore/<slug>`; PRs merged
  into `master`. 50 commits, 15 PRs at time of crawl.
- Commit subjects are sentences describing the change's *effect*, not conventional-commit
  prefixes — e.g. "Wire act modifierBonuses into computeModifiers — Act IV was drafting adults".
- `node_modules` is tracked as a **symlink** (mode 120000) and currently shows as deleted in
  `git status`. This is pre-existing; do not stage that deletion. Stage `src/` explicitly.
